title: Kogoro Mouri's Imposter
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector-equivalent Detective Yamamura of Gunma Prefecture Police) omitted by convention. case_type: murder. Two-part episode; both transcripts read in full. The old wiki-derived case file at cases/ep243-244_kogoro_mouris_imposter.json correctly identified Jinbo (s2) as the culprit, but mischaracterized the 5-years-ago crime as 'embezzlement' when the transcript is explicit it was extortion/blackmail against a confectionery company ('two men threatened a confectionery company and stole 100 million yen'). It also completely omitted the unrelated 4-years-ago forest suicide victim (here p6) whose milk carton, red bean bread, cigarettes and convenience-store receipt Jinbo scavenged and planted on the long-haired man's remains -- this fake-time-of-death trick (not a fake-identity trick, as the old file's object o1 description implied) is the mechanical core of Jinbo's alibi and had to be modeled with its own backstory victim and provenance chain. The old file also had no witness/backstory nodes for Onda or Urakawa beyond generic suspect stubs, missed the red-herring accusation Kogoro briefly levels at Onda, and missed both resolving clues (the Ran-Mouri-labeled cell phone handed over without hesitation, and the dusty old fingerprints vs. fresh footprints on the shogi board/desk). murderer_id in label matches the old file's s2 (Jinbo) -- transcript confirms this, no discrepancy to document there.

clues.desc: When Jinbo returns Ran's cell phone (found in Kogoro's car) directly to the real Kogoro without a moment's hesitation or asking which of the two men it belongs to -- reading the 'Ran Mouri' sticker and matching daughter to father instantly -- it contradicts his claim of never having seen the real Kogoro's face before; he could only know this because he'd already distinguished the real Kogoro from the imposter he hired.

Jinbo's fingerprints on Room 209's light bulb are old and buried under a thick layer of dust (consistent with a long-past light-bulb change), while his bare footprints on the shogi board and desk beneath the ceiling beam are fresh -- no inn would let a light collect that much dust while otherwise keeping the room clean, so the footprints must date to the murder, not the innocent light-changing excuse he offers.
